title: 100 Emails
comparison: ~20 kg/year if you send 10000 emails
comment: Most of that footprint comes from the data centres storing and routing your messages — not your device

title: 10 Hour Streaming
comparison: Streaming accounts for ~80% of internet traffic
comment: Digital sector produces 4% of GHG projected to reach 14% by 2040

title: 1 Banana
comparison: ~20 kg/year eating one every second day
comment: One of the lowest-footprint foods you can buy — bananas travel by ship not plane and need no packaging

title: 1kg Potatoes
comparison: ~25kg/year in average per person in Ireland
comment: On average, people in Ireland eat between 85 kg and 96 kg of potatoes per person every year.

title: 1 Bag of Tayto
comparison: ~6 kg/year if you have one every day
comment: Crisp production is energy-intensive; packaging adds to footprint

title: 1 Pint of Guinness
comparison: ~30 kg/year for a pint a day
comment: Diageo has committed to net zero operations by 2030

title: 1kg Irish Butter
comparison: ~33 kg/year at typical household use
comment: Irish dairy has one of the lower emissions intensities in Europe but is still significant

title: 1kg Cheddar Cheese
comparison: Cheese requires ~10L of milk per kg
comment: Dairy is Ireland's biggest agricultural emission source

title: 1kg Chicken
comparison: Chicken has ~10x lower footprint than beef; still significantly higher than plant protein
comment: Chicken is one of the better meat choices for the climate — but lentils or beans have a 10x lower footprint again

title: 1 Litre Oat Milk
comparison: vs ~3.2 kg for cow's milk
comment: Oat milk uses ~80% less land and ~60% less water than dairy milk

title: 1 Litre Cow's Milk
comparison: ~1.2 t/year for a family of 4 drinking 1L/day
comment: Ireland is one of Europe's largest dairy exporters

title: 1 Washing Load
comparison: Most emissions come from the energy to warm up the water
comment: Washing at 30°C instead of 40°C cuts energy use by about 40% — and modern detergents work just as well

title: 10 Min Shower
comparison: ~760 kg CO₂/year if you shower daily
comment: Cutting a 10-minute shower to 4 minutes roughly halves the footprint — and saves on hot water bills too

title: 1 Tumble Dryer Load
comparison: ~280 kg/year if used daily
comment: Air drying clothes saves the full amount; dryers are among the most energy-hungry home appliances

title: 1 Dishwasher Cycle
comparison: Similar footprint to a washing machine load at 40°C
comment: Roughly equivalent to a washing machine load; newer A-rated models use significantly less energy

title: Heating Home 1 Day
comparison: ~4400 kg/year for a typical Irish home
comment: Over half of Irish homes use gas or oil for heating; heat pumps cut this by 50-70%

title: LED Bulb vs Halogen
comparison: Switching all bulbs in a home saves ~80 kg/year
comment: LED uses ~80% less energy; halogen bulbs are now banned for sale in the EU

title: 1 Pizza
comparison: ~78 kg/year if you eat one every week
comment: The cheese topping accounts for nearly half the pizza's total footprint

title: 1 Cheeseburger
comparison: ~166 kg/year if eaten weekly
comment: The beef patty alone accounts for over 70% of the footprint — the bun and packaging are a tiny fraction

title: 100km by Train
comparison: About 4x less than the same trip by car
comment: Irish Rail has committed to full electrification by 2030 — the footprint will fall further as the grid gets greener

title: 1kg of Coffee Beans
comparison: ~180 kg/year at 1 kg/month
comment: Coffee production requires significant water consumption
action_title: Switch to a certified sustainable coffee brand
action_desc: Look for Rainforest Alliance or organic certification next time you buy beans or ground coffee.
action_saving: Reduces water use and land pressure per kg of beans

title: 100km by Car
comparison: ~4000 kg/year at 16000 km driven
comment: Excludes manufacturing; also causes local air pollution and health impacts
action_title: Replace one car journey with public transport this week
action_desc: Even one return trip by bus or train instead of car saves roughly 50 kg CO₂ over the year if done weekly.
action_saving: ~50 kg CO₂ saved/year if done weekly

title: 1kg Lamb
comparison: ~365 kg/year for someone eating lamb once a week
comment: Sheep produce more methane relative to their size than cattle — which is why lamb often has a higher footprint per kg than beef
action_title: Try one lamb-free week this month
action_desc: Lamb has one of the highest footprints of any meat. Swapping it for chicken or legumes makes a real difference.
action_saving: ~28 kg CO₂ saved per kg avoided

title: 1 Pair Leather Shoes
comparison: Same as driving a petrol car about 120 km
comment: The tanning process for leather is highly polluting; most leather is a by-product of the beef industry
action_title: Buy your next pair of shoes second-hand or from a sustainable brand
action_desc: Manufacturing one pair of leather shoes produces ~30 kg CO₂. Second-hand or vegan alternatives cut that dramatically.
action_saving: Up to 30 kg CO₂ saved per pair

title: 1 Fast Fashion T-Shirt
comparison: Same as leaving a phone charger plugged in for 6 months
comment: ~96% of cotton is grown with pesticides; fast fashion creates 92M tonnes of waste per year

title: 1 Pair of Jeans
comparison: Same footprint as driving ~130 km in a petrol car
comment: Takes ~7500 litres of water to produce one pair; equivalent to ~7 years of drinking water

title: 1kg Beef
comparison: ~3 kg CO₂ per 100g serving — like leaving a laptop running for a week
comment: Beef and dairy together account for roughly 65% of all agricultural greenhouse gas emissions globally
action_desc: Beef is the highest-impact common food. Replacing it with chicken, fish or plant protein just once a week adds up.
action_saving: ~60 kg CO₂ saved per kg avoided

title: 1 Smartphone
comparison: Same as charging your phone every day for 185 years
comment: About 80% of a phone's lifetime footprint comes from manufacturing — not from using it
action_title: Keep your current phone for one more year
action_desc: Manufacturing a new smartphone produces ~70 kg CO₂. The best phone for the planet is the one you already own.

title: 1 Bicycle
comparison: Same as a return Dublin–Belfast train journey
comment: Manufacturing is the main footprint — once built a bike produces zero emissions per km
action_desc: Manufacturing a new bicycle uses ~96 kg CO₂. Second-hand bikes cut that to near zero — and save money too.

title: Dublin–Holyhead Ferry
comparison: A return flight Dublin–Manchester emits ~3x more CO₂
comment: Ferry + train to the UK is often competitive in time once you factor in airport check-in — and far lower carbon

title: 1 Rasher of Bacon
comparison: ~18 kg/year for one rasher per day
comment: Pork has a lower footprint than beef or lamb but still 4x higher than chicken per kg

title: 1 New Electric Car
comparison: ~3x lower lifetime emissions than a new petrol car
comment: EVs break even vs petrol cars after ~2-3 years of use; lifetime emissions still significantly lower

title: Paris Olympics Visit
comparison: 1.6 Mt total for 13-16M visitors
comment: Lower than Tokyo; half of London Olympics impact
action_title: Choose a local or low-travel event for your next big trip
action_desc: A single major sporting event visit can cost 125 kg CO₂. Choosing an event within driving distance makes a big difference.
action_saving: ~125 kg CO₂ saved per trip avoided

title: 1 Laptop
comparison: Same as flying Dublin to London and back
comment: About 75% of a laptop's total footprint happens during manufacturing — before you even switch it on
action_title: Repair or refurbish your laptop instead of buying new
action_desc: A new laptop produces ~300 kg CO₂ in manufacturing alone. Most repairs cost a fraction of that — and extend its life by years.

title: Dublin–Madrid Flight
comparison: 2.2 tonnes/year for 4 yearly trips
comment: Aviation represents 2.5% of global emissions; very inequitably distributed
action_title: Replace one short-haul flight with a train or ferry
action_desc: A return Dublin–Madrid flight produces ~550 kg CO₂. For journeys under 5–6 hours, train is usually feasible and far lower impact.

title: 1 Year Digital Life
comparison: 1844 kg/year for a 2.9-person household
comment: Digital sector produces 4% of GHG projected to reach 14% by 2040
action_title: Enable downloads instead of streaming this week
action_desc: Streaming constantly uses data centres. Downloading music or videos on Wi-Fi, then watching offline, cuts that energy use significantly.
action_saving: Part of your ~636 kg/year digital footprint

title: 1 Year Pet Dog
comparison: Similar to a return flight from Dublin to New York
comment: Most of a dog's footprint comes from their meat-based food — switching to a lower-carbon brand makes a real difference
action_title: Switch your dog to a lower-impact food brand
action_desc: A dog's annual footprint is ~770 kg CO₂, mostly from meat-based food. Several brands now offer lower-carbon recipes with insect or plant protein.

title: 1 Ton Cement
comparison: ~200 kg for a 10 m² terrace (10 cm thick)
comment: Cement production accounts for about 8% of global CO₂ emissions — more than all the world's trucks combined
action_title: Ask about lower-carbon materials for your next home project
action_desc: Cement production is highly carbon-intensive. For patios, paths or small builds, alternatives like recycled aggregate or timber can be used.

title: 1 Year Food Waste
comparison: ~30% of food is wasted
comment: Waste generates methane; a major impact-reduction opportunity
action_title: Plan your meals this week to reduce food waste
action_desc: The average household wastes enough food to produce 1,600 kg CO₂ a year. A simple weekly plan and checking your fridge before shopping can cut that by half.

title: NY–London Flight
comparison: Business class is even higher
comment: Aviation represents 2.5% of global emissions; very inequitably distributed
action_title: Offset your next long-haul flight — and consider flying less
action_desc: A return NY–London flight produces ~1,800 kg CO₂. High-quality carbon offsets through Gold Standard can neutralise that while you reduce flying long-term.

title: $10K in a Dirty Bank
comparison: More than flying return from Dublin to Australia
comment: 20-30% of bank lending goes to carbon-intensive industry
action_title: Check if your bank funds fossil fuels — and consider switching
action_desc: €10K in a fossil-fuel-lending bank generates ~2,400 kg CO₂/year through loans. Green banks like Triodos exist and are fully regulated.

title: New Small Car
comparison: Same as an average Irish person's entire carbon footprint for 5 months
comment: Even the smallest new car carries a large manufacturing footprint — second-hand is always the lower-carbon choice
action_title: Consider a second-hand or electric car for your next purchase
action_desc: Manufacturing a new small car produces ~4,000 kg CO₂. Buying second-hand avoids that entirely. EVs have a lower lifetime footprint even accounting for the battery.
action_saving: ~4000 kg CO₂ saved vs. new petrol car

title: New Range Rover
comparison: Same as heating an Irish home for nearly 6 years
comment: One of the highest manufacturing footprints of any consumer product you can buy
action_title: Consider a smaller second-hand or electric vehicle next time
action_desc: A new Range Rover produces ~25,000 kg CO₂ in manufacturing — one of the highest of any consumer product. Even a new mid-size EV is dramatically lower.
action_saving: ~20000+ kg CO₂ saved vs. new large SUV

title: 1kg Asparagus
comparison: Flown from Peru it jumps to ~12 kg CO₂ — 30x higher
comment: Asparagus is often imported out of season; shipped from Peru it rises to 0.67 kg but flown it can reach almost 12 kg
